classification.difficultyReason: Calculate the vertical climb and compare the resulting altitude with the mountain height.

content.prompt:
A plane flying at $1850$ m starts to climb at an angle of $18^{\circ}$ to the horizontal when the pilot sees a mountain peak $2450$ m high, $2600$ m away from him in a horizontal direction.

Will the pilot clear the mountain? Give the clearance to $1$ decimal place.

spec.description: Unshaded mountain outline with the plane's starting position at the left. Dashed horizontal and rising reference lines meet the mountain height line; the source rising line towards the peak is schematic rather than a calculated flight endpoint. Decorative aeroplane artwork is replaced by an editable plane label.
spec.mathematics: Starting altitude 1850 m, mountain height 2450 m, horizontal distance 2600 m and climb angle 18 degrees. Right-angle marker between the horizontal reference and mountain vertical.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated altitude or clearance is shown.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the vertical climb after travelling $2600$ m horizontally.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 18^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{2600}\\h&=2600\tan 18^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
The clearance above the peak is
$$\begin{align*}c&=1850+2600\tan 18^{\circ}-2450\\c&\approx244.8\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The clearance is positive, so the plane clears the mountain by $244.8$ m.
